candidates.computation_change_reason: The dissolved manganese form selects which parameter-specific numeric limits (A), monitoring requirements (B), and missing-result classifications (C) apply; conflating it with total manganese or another speciation would change matched obligations and limit comparisons.

These repeated numerics appear in a row whose column meanings are not defined in the segment; if any instance is read as an enforceable effluent or water-quality-based limit rather than a non-operative calculated or background value, the applicable discharge limit and exceedance determination for reported measurements would change.

The sentinel-like magnitude may indicate no numeric limit, a non-binding placeholder, or an effectively unbounded value rather than a literal compliance threshold; treating it as a real enforceable limit versus a marker of non-applicability changes whether numeric compliance comparison is performed.

These larger calculated values sit alongside smaller repeated figures in the same row; interpreting them as operative discharge limits rather than reasonable-potential or statistical outputs would alter which numeric threshold governs exceedance analysis.

Without column headers in the segment, this token could encode monitoring frequency, sample size, permit limit identifier, or another schedule attribute; a different reading changes whether a monitoring obligation was actually applicable in FY2025.

The terminal N/A may denote conditional monitoring not required, a documented no-discharge or no-data state, or simply that no numeric comparison applies; each reading yields a different monitoring-obligation outcome (B) and a different missing-evidence classification (C) for periods without ordinary numeric results.
